colorRules.accentUsage: Use Wavelength's deep teal accent as a purposeful action and orientation color: primary CTAs, selected navigation states, links, focus rings, progress indicators, key financial deltas, and occasional compact badges. Keep accent usage to roughly 3–7 visible instances per screen so actions remain easy to scan. Use the strongest accent shade for high-contrast controls and darker accent shades for text on light surfaces; reserve lighter shades for subtle fills and selected-row states.
colorRules.semanticUsage: Use success, warning, danger, and info as restrained semantic signals rather than decorative colors. Prefer tinted backgrounds with appropriately dark text, compact badges, and 1px status borders; use semantic text directly only when contrast is reliable. Success should communicate positive cash flow or completed actions, warning should flag upcoming bills or low balances, danger should identify failed payments or overdrafts, and info should explain unfamiliar financial concepts. Semantic colors must not compete with the primary teal action color.
colorRules.neutralUsage: Build hierarchy from the neutral scale and the pale green-tinted surfaces: the lightest neutral steps support the app background and raised panels, mid-light steps define subtle dividers and secondary surfaces, and the darkest neutral steps serve primary text and high-priority numbers. Use the provided primary text for headings and balances, secondary text for supporting explanations, muted text for metadata and helper copy, and the strongest border neutral only where separation is necessary. Maintain a soft, calm contrast appropriate for a beginner-friendly fintech product.
forbiddenPatterns: Do not use more than one accent hue in a screen or introduce unrelated blue, purple, or red accents outside semantic states.
Do not use the teal accent as a large decorative background, full-page wash, or heavy illustration fill.
Do not use gradients on cards, sections, controls, or data surfaces.
Do not use pure black or pure white; preserve the warm green-tinted neutral system.
Do not communicate financial status with color alone; pair semantic color with labels, icons, or explicit values.

typographyRules.displayUsage: Use Sora for the Wavelength wordmark, page titles, section headings, prominent balances, and short onboarding statements. Its geometric character should make money management feel bold and approachable without turning the interface into a novelty product. Keep display text left-aligned in app layouts and use it selectively for hierarchy.
typographyRules.bodyUsage: Use DM Sans for body copy, navigation labels, form fields, buttons, tables, transaction descriptions, explanatory finance copy, and supporting metadata. It should carry most of the interface because its clarity suits users who are learning financial terminology. Keep body text conversational, concise, and at least 16px for primary reading content.
typographyRules.monoUsage: Use IBM Plex Mono for account identifiers, transaction IDs, reference codes, timestamps where precision matters, tabular figures requiring column alignment, and technical or export-oriented labels. Do not use it for general headings, long-form explanation, or primary navigation.
typographyRules.weightRules: Use 400 for body copy and ordinary data, 500 for labels, navigation, and control text, 600 for emphasis, balances, table headers, and important financial states, and 700 sparingly for major page titles or hero-scale numeric emphasis. Headings may range from 600–700; never use 200, 300, 800, or 900, and never bold entire paragraphs.
typographyRules.sizeRules: Use 16px/24px as the minimum body size and 14px/20px only for compact metadata, table support text, and secondary labels. Use 12px/16px for captions and micro-status text only when nonessential. Use 20–24px for component headings, 30–36px for page headings, and 48px/52px for occasional prominent balance or onboarding emphasis. Keep long-form copy at 16–18px with comfortable line height.

spacingRules.sectionMargins: Use a centered max-width container designed for 1280px, with app content organized as sidebar plus main workspace rather than a centered hero. Separate major workspace sections with 48–96px vertical spacing depending on importance; use 32–48px between subsections. Vary section heights intentionally and avoid repeating identical vertical gaps.
spacingRules.componentPadding: Use 16px horizontal and 12px vertical padding for compact controls, navigation rows, and dense transaction items. Use 24px horizontal and 16px vertical padding for relaxed panels, forms, and summary regions. Use 32px padding for primary workspace surfaces or important empty states, while preserving tighter spacing inside data tables.
spacingRules.rhythmDescription: Use an airy but balanced 4px-based token system with an evident 8px rhythm. Prioritize scanability for first-time money managers: generous space around balances and decisions, compact rows for repeated transactions, and clear grouping through spacing before relying on borders or cards.

motionRules.transitions: Use color and border transitions for hover, focus, selected, validation, and semantic state changes. Use small opacity transitions for tooltips, notices, and progressive reveals. Use restrained transform transitions for drawers, menus, and layout changes; avoid decorative bouncing, parallax, and motion that suggests financial volatility. Respect reduced-motion preferences.
motionRules.easing: Use the standard smooth cubic-bezier curve for predictable movement that starts decisively and settles cleanly. Motion should feel playful through timing and clarity, not through spring-heavy overshoot or ornamental effects.
motionRules.duration: Use 120ms for hover, pressed, focus, and icon-state feedback; 200ms for control state changes, menus, validation, and row updates; and 320ms for drawers, page-level transitions, and larger workspace reveals. Keep financial confirmations immediate and never delay a critical status message for animation.

signatureMoves: Lead key screens with a bold Sora financial figure or balance, paired with a short plain-language explanation rather than a decorative hero.
Use deep teal as a disciplined action-and-orientation thread across primary controls, selected sidebar items, focus rings, and a small number of financial highlights.
Present money activity as highly scannable rows and compact tables with clear merchant, date, amount, and status hierarchy instead of card-heavy dashboards.
Use pale green-tinted raised surfaces, subtle borders, and generous whitespace to make financial information feel calm, approachable, and trustworthy.
Pair playful, human microcopy with precise mono-spaced identifiers and aligned numbers, balancing personality with fintech-grade clarity.
antiPatterns: Never use centered marketing-style hero layouts inside the app; use a functional sidebar and content workspace.
Never build the primary dashboard from a grid of more than three cards; prefer lists, tables, summaries, and purposeful panels.
Never use gradient hero sections, floating blobs, abstract decorative shapes, or ornamental background patterns.
Never rely on circular-avatar testimonial carousels, vague finance clichés, or generic AI-sounding copy.
Never obscure balances, fees, due dates, or transaction status behind playful animation, low-contrast styling, or color-only indicators.
